title: Ops capacity scenarios & embedded pricing hedge plan (2029)
summary: Working sheet that combines capacity/headcount scenarios with an embedded pricing hedge design. Purpose: recommend a blended commit + burst credit mix and hiring triggers that keep unit cost within target bands while preserving latency SLAs for Q1-Q4 2029.
assumptions:
- Revenue growth shaped by PLG conversion curve: 35% YoY ARR growth in base, 55% in upside, 10% in downside.
- Average tokens per active session: 1,100 (SD 320).
- Baseline per-token hosted cost (variable infra + licensing) = $0.00028 in current config; reserved capacity reduces variable cost by up to 40% at high utilization.
- Burst (spot) capacity available up to 25% of peak for variable discount but with throughput variability.
- Hiring lead time: 8 weeks from offer to full productivity for infra/ops roles.
- Headcount ramp wages and overhead included in model at blended fully-loaded cost of $305k per head/year for infra-engineering and $220k for finance/ops support.
- SLAs: p50 latency <= 180ms; p95 <= 850ms for standard routes.

monte_carlo_summary: Ran 10k-sample Monte Carlo across demand volatility (sigma=22%), spot-burst availability (uniform 0-30%), and reserved utilization elasticity. Median unit cost change vs deterministic base: +4.6%. 90th percentile downside shows unit cost +28% -> indicates need for protective hedges (convertible credits or flexible short-term reserved windows). Simulation files: CON-8462 (confluence) contains full outputs.
headcount_plan_summary: Proposed hires (constrained budget path): Q1 2029: 3 infra engineers (service/runtime tuning), 1 infra SRE, 1 capacity planner; Q2: 2 infra engineers, 1 solutions engineer; Q3: pause hiring unless utilization > 0.72 for trailing 8 weeks; Q4: scale hiring aggressively in upside scenario with +6 infra hires to support new customers. Net additional headcount by year-end (base) = +7 FTEs. Cost impact baked into net-op-ex lines above.
pricing_sensitivity_notes: Key sensitivities identified: per-token price moves (our public price) vs committed revenue: -10% price drop increases committed coverage gap and moves utilization down by ~8 p.p., pushing unit-cost +12%. CPU/GPU price volatility (cloud spot pricing) is large driver of tail-case cost. Recommendation: define 3 price bands for public offering with auto-adjust rules tied to trailing 14-day unit-cost rolling average and a reserve-to-burst reallocation protocol.
recommended_triggers:
- Trigger A (Scale reserved): sustained 7-day avg utilization >= 0.72 => auto-approve additional 10% reserved commit.
- Trigger B (Pause hiring): trailing 8-week utilization <= 0.50 and 30-day ARR delta <= -3% => freeze non-critical hires.
- Trigger C (Activate hedges): Monte Carlo 90th percentile unit-cost > 1.2x baseline => purchase short-window convertible reserved blocks (30-90 days) up to 15% of forecasted peak.
- Trigger D (Price action): if unit-cost drift > +8% for 14 days, initiate price band shift (notify growth + legal) and enable graceful degradation routing to cheaper model variants for non-SLA routes.
decisions_for_exec: 1) Approve initial blended hedge: 55% reserved / 15% burst (base). 2) Pre-approve $1.2M budget for short-window convertible reserved blocks for tail-risk protection. 3) Authorize hiring plan with stop/go triggers described. 4) Mandate integration of trailing-unit-cost metric into Console (ops) for automated routing decisions.
